# Technical Analysis Report: TEAM (Atlassian Corporation) — as of 2026-10-12

## Indicator Selection Rationale

I selected 8 complementary indicators covering trend, momentum, volatility, and price structure: **close_50_sma** (medium-term trend), **close_200_sma** (long-term trend benchmark), **close_10_ema** (short-term momentum/entry timing), **macd** + **macdh** (trend momentum and its acceleration; macds is redundant with macdh which directly measures the MACD–signal gap), **rsi** (overbought/oversold), **boll_ub** (volatility envelope upper boundary), and **atr** (volatility-based risk sizing). This set avoids redundancy while covering all four analytical dimensions.

## Trend Structure: Powerful Uptrend Across All Timeframes

TEAM closed at **$207.75** on 2026-10-12 (high $212.84, low $205.43, volume 1.98M — relatively light). The moving-average stack is textbook bullish:

- Price ($207.75) >> 10 EMA ($197.52) >> 50 SMA ($175.98) >> 200 SMA ($113.51)
- Price sits **~83% above its 200 SMA** — an extraordinary extension reflecting the dramatic regime change that occurred in early August, when the stock gapped from ~$110 (2026-08-06 close: $110.17) to ~$149 (2026-08-07 close: $149.07) on a massive volume spike (20.1M shares vs. a typical 2–6M). That single session re-rated the stock ~35% and it has not looked back.
- The 50 SMA ($175.98) crossed and remains far above the 200 SMA ($113.51), and both are still rising — a confirmed long-term bullish regime, not a short squeeze fading out.

## Recent Price Action: Breakout After a Shallow Correction

After peaking at $195.67 on 2026-09-21, TEAM corrected ~10% into a $175.96 low on 2026-09-29 — notably holding right at the rising 50 SMA zone (~$156–176 range at that time, and the Bollinger lower band now at $175.34). The September pullback was orderly: RSI bottomed at ~47.7 (2026-09-29), never approaching oversold, which signals dip-buying rather than distribution.

Since 2026-10-01 ($189.91), the stock has rallied seven of the last eight sessions: $203.57 → $206.79 → $207.75, with the 2026-10-12 intraday high of $212.84 marking the highest level in the visible dataset (above the prior August peak of ~$197.30 high on 2026-08-31). This is a clean breakout to new highs.

## Momentum: Re-accelerating After Reset

- **MACD** at 7.79, rising sharply from 5.15 (2026-10-02) — the MACD line had fallen from a mid-September peak of ~13.6 during the correction and has now turned back up decisively.
- **MACD Histogram** flipped positive on 2026-10-09 (+0.43) and expanded to +0.79 on 2026-10-12 — a fresh bullish crossover after a 3-week negative stretch. This is a classic "momentum reset and re-acceleration" pattern that often precedes trend continuation.
- **RSI** at 66.74 — bullish but not yet overbought (70 threshold). It has room to expand before signaling exhaustion, though it is approaching the zone where prior rallies (mid-September, RSI ~67.7) stalled.

## Volatility and Band Position: Pressing the Upper Band

- **Bollinger upper band** at 208.71; the close at $207.75 sits just beneath it, and the intraday high ($212.84) exceeded it. Riding/piercing the upper band in a strong trend is normal, but the position is stretched short-term — mean-reversion pullbacks toward the middle band ($192.03) are the usual cost of entry at band extremes.
- **ATR** at 8.48 (~4.1% of price) and declining from ~9.4 in late September — volatility is contracting into the breakout, which is constructive. However, an ATR of ~$8.50 means daily swings of ±4% are routine; position sizing must account for this.

## Actionable Insights

- **Trend traders**: The bias is unambiguously long while price holds above the 10 EMA ($197.52). The bullish MACD histogram crossover (2026-10-09) supports continuation.
- **Entry discipline**: Buying at the upper Bollinger band after a 7-of-8-day run carries poor short-term reward/risk. A pullback toward the 10 EMA (~$197.50) or the Bollinger midline (~$192) would offer a better entry aligned with the trend. The September low ($175.96) and 50 SMA (~$176) define the deeper invalidation zone.
- **Risk management**: With ATR ~$8.50, a 1×ATR stop implies roughly a $197 stop (10 EMA confluence); a 2×ATR stop near $190 sits just below the Bollinger midline — both defensible levels.
- **Caution flag**: Volume on the latest breakout sessions (~2M shares) is well below the August breakout volume and below the September decline days (~3–6M). Breakouts on light volume are more prone to failure — watch for volume confirmation or a failed retest of $200.

## Summary Table

| Long-term trend | Strongly bullish | Close $207.75 vs 200 SMA $113.51 (+83%) |
| Medium trend | Bullish | Close vs 50 SMA $175.98; 50 SMA rising, golden-cross structure |

| Overbought/oversold | Neutral-bullish | RSI 66.74, below 70; prior stall at ~67.7 on 09-21 |
| Band position | Stretched | Close $207.75 just under boll_ub $208.71; midline $192.03 |
| Volatility | Contracting | ATR 8.48 (~4.1%), down from ~9.4 late Sept |

## Sentiment Report: TEAM (Atlassian), 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-12

### 1. Source-by-source breakdown

**Yahoo Finance news — unavailable.** The feed returned a placeholder: Yahoo only serves recent items, so this is a data gap, not an absence of news. No institutional/fact-driven signal could be sampled this week.

**StockTwits — modest sample, mildly bullish lean.** 30 messages: 4 Bullish (13%), 3 Bearish (10%), 23 unlabeled. The labeled ratio is 4:3 — close to neutral — but the unlabeled message bodies skew constructive:
- Multiple breakout/momentum observations: '$TEAM printed a new 52-week high today' (appears twice, 10-08 and 10-12), 'Clean breakout on daily and weekly', 'Stock breaking key level of $200 on the daily... looking for $215 and $225', '200 breakout on volume for trigger'.

- Bearish counterweight is narrow: all 3 Bearish tags come from a single account (@Johannes0678) posting short-term chart levels — 'great.... 200 dollar is coming' reads as expecting a pullback to $200 support, not a thesis-level short.
- Notable skepticism among unlabeled posts: one user flags $TEAM among 'overvalued af' software names; another plans to exit remaining shares at ~$300 cost basis after the '2021 interest rate disaster' — scar tissue from prior cycles, not fresh bearishness.

**Reddit — thin and largely incidental.** 5 posts mentioning TEAM, none with TEAM as the subject: an r/wallstreetbets macro-bear post, a data-centers-in-space thesis, an ADBE bear post (competitive read-across to software multiples), a meme-stock weekly thread, and a South Korea AI program post on r/stocks. r/investing returned nothing. No vote/comment counts are provided, so engagement cannot be inferred. Reddit offers no directional signal on TEAM itself.

### 2. Cross-source divergences and alignments

News is unavailable, so no divergence can be measured there. Within StockTwits there is a mild divergence: labeled tags are nearly balanced (4B/3Br) while the unlabeled content is clearly momentum-positive — the classifier-style read would be more bullish than the tag ratio suggests. Reddit is silent on TEAM specifically, meaning the retail-momentum story on StockTwits is not being echoed by broader community discussion — a niche rather than crowd-wide signal.

### 3. Dominant narrative themes

- **Breakout / 52-week highs / $200 level reclaim.** The single dominant theme: TEAM breaking and holding above $200, with traders eyeing $215–$225 next.
- **Software sector rotation.** Multiple posts group TEAM with $MDB $SNOW $DDOG $CRM $NOW — a software-momentum basket trade.
- **Post-earnings follow-through.** One thread debates whether the stock holds post-earnings gains this cycle vs. the usual dump-then-spike pattern.
- **Valuation scar tissue.** A minority theme: 2021-era bagholders and 'overvalued software' framing tempering the momentum enthusiasm.

### 4. Catalysts and risks

- **Catalysts:** new 52-week highs attracting momentum screens and breakout-buyer attention; reported IBD SwingTrader buy mention; post-earnings strength continuing without the expected pullback; potential S&P inclusion speculation ('add this thing to the S&P').
- **Risks:** the $200 level is now the line in the sand — failure to hold it flips the breakout narrative quickly; clustered '52-week high' euphoria is a mild over-extension signal; valuation skepticism persists even among holders; no hard news flow this week means the move is technically driven and lacks an institutional-news anchor. No upcoming dated catalyst (e.g., earnings date) appears in the data.

# TEAM (Atlassian Corporation) — Fundamental Analysis Report
## As of 2026-10-12

### Data Caveats
- Profile fundamentals (market cap, multiples, 52-week range, sector/industry labels) are withheld by the vendor for this date — no current-day values are served back to 2026-10-12. All statement data below is point-in-time SEC EDGAR facts as filed on or before 2026-10-12.
- Insider transactions are withheld — the vendor cannot establish which trades were publicly known as of 2026-10-12.
- TEAM reports on a June fiscal year-end; the latest available quarter is FY2026 Q4 ended 2026-06-30 (balance sheet) with income/cash flow through FY2026 Q3 ended 2026-03-31.

### Revenue & Growth
Revenue has compounded steadily every quarter in the dataset:

- 2021-09-30: $614M → 2023-09-30: $978M → 2024-09-30: $1,188M → 2025-09-30: $1,433M → 2026-03-31: $1,787M
- YoY growth on comparable quarters: ~22% (Sep-23 vs Sep-22), ~21% (Sep-24 vs Sep-23), ~21% (Sep-25 vs Sep-24). Mar-26 vs Mar-25: +32% ($1,787M vs $1,357M).
- Dec-25 quarter revenue of $1,586M and Mar-26 of $1,787M show growth re-accelerating, not decelerating — cloud/subscription mix continues to drive expansion.

### Margins & Profitability
- Gross margin is elite and improving: ~85% in Mar-26 ($1,524M gross profit on $1,787M revenue) vs ~84% a year earlier.
- Operating income remains negative in most recent quarters: -$48M (Dec-25), -$56M (Mar-26), -$96M (Sep-25). TEAM continues to invest heavily (R&D + SBC) ahead of GAAP profitability.
- Net income: -$98M in Mar-26, -$43M in Dec-25, -$52M in Sep-25. Diluted EPS: -$0.38 (Mar-26), -$0.16 (Dec-25).
- Structural note: Q1 fiscal year (Sep quarter) is seasonally the weakest for opex vs revenue; the business consistently shows operating losses but strong cash generation — losses are largely driven by non-cash stock-based compensation.

### Cash Flow — The Real Story
- Operating cash flow is robust and seasonal (Mar quarter is the strongest, likely annual billing cycles): $653M (Mar-25), $567M (Mar-26), $352M (Dec-24).
- Capex is negligible ($6–14M/quarter) — asset-light software model; nearly all OCF converts to FCF.
- FY ending ~Mar-26 TTM OCF ≈ $567 + $178 + $129 + $653 ≈ $1.53B — the market should value TEAM on FCF, not GAAP EPS.
- Notable items: Dec-25 shows -$1,144M investing outflow and -$991M financing outflow — large cash deployment (acquisition/investment + buyback or debt repayment). Cash fell from $2,322M (Sep-25) to $1,158M (Dec-25), consistent with a major capital return or M&A event in that quarter.

### Balance Sheet
- Total assets: $6,104M (Jun-26); stockholders equity recovered to $1,058M after dipping to $879M (Mar-26) — the Dec-25 cash deployment compressed equity temporarily.
- Cash: $1,240M at Jun-26 (rebuilt from $1,158M at Dec-25 via strong OCF).
- Current liabilities ($3,571M at Jun-26) exceed current assets ($2,797M) — normal for subscription software (large deferred revenue), not a solvency concern. Equity has grown from $567M (2020) to $1,058M (2026), and was negative in 2021 — the equity base has materially strengthened.

### Trader Takeaways
- Growth quality: durable ~20%+ top-line growth with re-acceleration in early 2026; 85% gross margins.
- Profitability: GAAP losses are structural (SBC-heavy), but FCF is large and growing — watch OCF trajectory, not EPS.
- The Dec-25 quarter's ~$2.1B combined investing+financing outflow is the biggest single event in the data — traders should confirm whether it was a buyback, debt retirement, or acquisition, as it drove cash down ~50% sequentially before OCF rebuilt it.
- Watch: any slowdown below ~20% YoY revenue growth, rising cost of revenue (cloud hosting), and whether operating losses narrow toward breakeven as revenue scales.

| Revenue growth ~21% YoY, re-accelerating | Mar-26 $1,787M vs Mar-25 $1,357M (+32%) | Bullish |
| Gross margin ~85% and rising | $1,524M / $1,787M (Mar-26) | Bullish |

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case: TEAM (Atlassian Corporation) — 2026-10-12

Let me open this debate, because the bear hasn't spoken yet — and frankly, I'm not sure what they'll have left to say once the evidence is on the table. TEAM isn't just a stock riding a hot tape. It's a franchise that just re-rated 35% in a single session, held every gain for two months, and is now breaking out to all-time highs on a textbook momentum reset. Here's the case.

## Growth isn't slowing — it's re-accelerating

The bear's first move will be "growth stocks are dead in a high-rate world." Look at the actual numbers instead of the narrative. Revenue: $1,357M (Mar-25) → $1,787M (Mar-26). That's **+32% YoY** — up from a ~21% pace that had already compounded for years ($614M → $978M → $1,188M → $1,433M across the Sep quarters). This isn't a decelerating legacy vendor; growth *accelerated* in 2026, driven by cloud migration and the AI monetization layer (Rovo, Atlassian Intelligence) that the news report itself flags as "the narrative that could decouple it from pure rate beta."

## The FCF story the GAAP bears will conveniently ignore

Yes, GAAP operating income is negative — -$56M in Mar-26. The bear will wave that flag. But they'd be either ignorant or dishonest about *why*: it's stock-based compensation, a non-cash expense, in a business converting revenue to cash at elite efficiency. TTM operating cash flow is ~**$1.5B**. Capex is ~$10M per quarter — nearly everything converts to free cash flow. Gross margin is **~85% and rising**. The market learned this lesson with every great SaaS franchise of the last decade: value TEAM on FCF, and the "unprofitable" label evaporates. The Dec-25 ~$2.1B capital deployment compressed cash temporarily — and the balance sheet rebuilt it to $1,240M within two quarters purely through operations. That's what a cash machine looks like.

## Technicals: this is what institutional re-rating looks like

The bear will call the August gap from $110 to $149 "overdone." Here's what actually happened: a 20M-share repricing — real volume, real institutional participation — followed by **two months of holding those gains**, an orderly 10% correction that bottomed exactly at the rising 50 SMA with RSI never even reaching oversold (~47.7), and now a fresh breakout to new all-time highs at $212.84 with a bullish MACD histogram crossover on 10-09 that's still expanding. Price > 10 EMA > 50 SMA > 200 SMA, all rising. The September pullback was accumulation, not distribution — that's the signature of dip-buyers, not bagholders. The stock is +83% above its 200 SMA and the 200 SMA itself is still climbing.

## Even the skeptics' own data is bullish

The sentiment report is labeled "low confidence," but look at what it actually contains: all three Bearish tags come from **a single account** predicting a pullback to $200 — which the stock has already blown through. Meanwhile the unlabeled chatter shows 52-week-high prints, $215–$225 targets, an IBD SwingTrader mention, and even S&P 500 inclusion speculation — a real catalyst that would force index buying. Reddit's silence isn't bearish; it means this move hasn't hit retail euphoria yet. We're early in the crowd-recognition phase, not late.

## Preempting the bear's best arguments

- **"Rising yields kill high-multiple SaaS."** True for *profitless* long-duration stories. TEAM's $1.5B FCF is current-year cash, not a 2035 promise — it's one of the least duration-exposed growth names in software precisely because the cash flows are real today.
- **"GAAP losses."** Covered above — SBC optics on a business generating ~40%+ FCF margins at scale.
- **"Light-volume breakout."** The one honest technical caveat. But breakouts *into* earnings season on light volume frequently resolve with the catalyst itself supplying the volume. And the invalidation is clean: lose $200 and the 10 EMA at $197.5, and the thesis gets re-tested — roughly 4-5% of defined risk against a stock that just proved $175 is a floor.
- **"Valuation scar tissue / 'overvalued' software."** 2021-era software was overvalued at 30x+ sales with zero cash flow. TEAM trades on ~$7.1B annualized revenue run-rate with $1.5B FCF — a completely different animal.

## The setup

A +32% growth re-acceleration, 85% gross margins, $1.5B free cash flow, a balance sheet that rebuilds itself, a confirmed all-time-high breakout, momentum re-accelerating off a clean reset, and potential S&P inclusion as a kicker — all into an earnings catalyst that historically has *fueled* this stock's re-ratings. The bear can gripe about macro headwinds and light volume. The tape and the cash flow statement say otherwise.

**Verdict: TEAM is a high-conviction bullish setup. The $200 breakout is the line — hold above it, and $215–$225 is the near-term path, with earnings as the accelerant.**

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case: TEAM (Atlassian Corporation) — 2026-10-12

The bull just gave you a beautiful story about a 35% re-rating, $1.5B in free cash flow, and a "confirmed" breakout. Let me tell you what the same data says when you're not trying to sell it: this is a stock trading 83% above its 200-day average, on a breakout nobody showed up for, into a macro environment that is actively hostile to exactly this kind of asset, with a binary earnings event weeks away. That's not a setup — that's a trap wearing a setup's clothes.

## The extension problem the bull can't wave away

The bull cites "+83% above the 200 SMA" as evidence of strength. It's evidence of *extension*. Name me the risk/reward on buying a stock 83% above its long-term mean, closing a tick under its upper Bollinger band, after going 7-for-8 sessions up. The technical report — the bull's own favorite document — says it plainly: "Buying at the upper Bollinger band after a 7-of-8-day run carries poor short-term reward/risk." Even the friendly read says the correct entry was $197 or $192, which means the correct action at $207.75 is *waiting*, not buying. The bull is asking you to chase.

## The light-volume breakout is not a footnote — it's the whole tell

The bull admits the caveat then hand-waves it: "the catalyst will supply the volume." That's hope, not analysis. The August re-rating happened on **20.1M shares**. This breakout? **1.98M** — below even the September *decline* days at 3–6M. The single most important session of this entire move — new all-time highs — was met with a shrug from institutions. Compare that to the bull's own framing: "real volume, real institutional participation" is what made August legitimate. By that standard, October is illegitimate. A breakout to all-time highs on a tenth of the August volume isn't confirmation of the re-rating; it's a candidate for a failed breakout. And failed breakouts at all-time highs don't pull back politely to the 10 EMA — they trap the entire momentum cohort that's been piling in for eight straight days.

## The macro tape is a loaded gun pointed at this exact stock

The bull's rebuttal — "TEAM's cash flows are current-year, not 2035 promises" — sounds clever until you ask what multiple the market pays on those cash flows. The news report's own words: "rising discount rates are a direct valuation headwind for high-multiple SaaS names like TEAM." Global bond yields are surging, France is flagged as a stress point, tech is slumping into earnings season, oil is rising, and the prevailing narrative is literally "bubble-like stock valuations." TEAM just re-rated 35% *into* this environment on no confirmed company news — the vendor returned zero TEAM-specific headlines all week. The stock got more expensive while its discount rate got worse. That's not decoupling; that's divergence, and divergences resolve. Meanwhile the "AI narrative" the bull leans on — Rovo, Atlassian Intelligence — is doing exactly nothing to distinguish TEAM from a crowded software-momentum basket; the sentiment data shows it traded as a ticker in a list next to $MDB $SNOW $DDOG, not as a differentiated story.

## The fundamentals are real but the bull is rounding aggressively

Yes, Mar-26 showed +32% YoY. One quarter. The Sep-25 quarter grew ~21% — the same pace it's compounded for years. Re-acceleration is a *possibility*, not a confirmed trend, and the bull is extrapolating one print into a new regime. Second: GAAP losses aren't just "SBC optics" — SBC is a real transfer of value from shareholders to employees, quarter after quarter, and at TEAM's scale it's the primary reason "operating losses persist" in nearly every recent quarter. Calling a -$56M operating quarter irrelevant because it's non-cash is the 2021 argument in a trench coat; the sentiment data shows even *holders* carry that scar tissue ("overvalued af," the exit-at-$300 cost-basis post). Third — and the bull conspicuously glossed this — the Dec-25 quarter shows a **$2.1B unexplained cash deployment** that halved the cash balance in one quarter, and the fundamental report's own verdict is "verify event type." The bull asserts it was productive capital return. The data doesn't say that. It says cash dropped 50% and nobody in this dataset knows why. Buying at all-time highs on top of an unverified balance-sheet event is not diligence.

## The sentiment picture is thinner than the bull claims

"All three Bearish tags come from one account" — sure, but flip it: only **four** Bullish tags exist in a 30-message sample, the labeled ratio is 4:3 (neutral by any honest read), Reddit produced zero TEAM-focused posts, Yahoo news returned nothing, and the report itself is stamped **low confidence**. The bull calls Reddit silence "early in the crowd-recognition phase." It could equally be *nobody cares* — a niche momentum trade with no institutional news anchor and no retail amplification is fragile, not stealthy. And the dominant theme in that thin chatter — "new 52-week high," "$200 breakout" — is pure price-chasing euphoria. When the strongest retail signal is "it's going up," the marginal buyer is almost exhausted by definition.

## The earnings coin-flip cuts both ways — and the asymmetry is worse than the bull admits

The bull says earnings "historically fueled re-ratings." The same sentiment data flags the opposing pattern: "the usual dump-then-spike" debate, and the macro report warns that implied vol is rising into earnings kickoff. With RSI at 66.7 — right where the mid-September rally stalled at ~67.7 — the bar for a beat-and-raise big enough to extend an 83%-above-the-200SMA stock is enormous, while the bar for disappointment is "anything less than perfect."
